newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Palestinian violence cycle back on course.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Palestinian violence cycle back on course.

text.p: The cycle of Israeli-Palestinian violence geared up again after U.S. mediation efforts this week produced only partial results.
Israel arrested a Palestinian policeman who it said had fired at troops on Thursday. Palestinians denied the accusation which was sure to stir another round of acrimony.
Earlier, several Israeli border policemen were arrested on suspicion of severely beating two Palestinians who defied a closure to reach their jobs in the Jewish state.

Israel imposed the blockade on the West Bank and Gaza Strip after two suicide bombers killed 14 people in a Jerusalem market last month, plunging already strained Middle East peacemaking to a new low.
The attack prompted an emergency shuttle mission by U.S. envoy Dennis Ross who succeeded in getting Israelis and Palestinians to exchange security information.
But remarks by officials on both sides after Ross left on Wednesday indicated the severe crisis in trust had not been settled.
"How can you dance the tango alone? You need a partner who is ready to dance with you," Arafat told reporters after meeting Israeli peace activists and left-wing lawmakers in Ramallah.
"We say, 'Is this government really ready to work with us to preserve the peace process and protect it? Is it really ready to do so?' I am sorry to say the answer is no," he said.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accuses Arafat of being indirectly responsible for the attack by allowing Moslem militants to operate freely in areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip under his control since 1994.

"We have to say honestly after four years that during those four years the Palestinian Authority did not operate against these groups," said Netanyahu. "Their people walk around freely with weapons, they accumulate ammunition."

A spokesman in Washington said Secretary of State Madeleine Albright would come to the region in September for the first time in a bid to break the impasse but would make additional stops and address other regional issues.

The Palestinian Wafa news agency said Albright telephoned Arafat late on Thursday to discuss results of the Ross mission. Arafat told her the Israeli closure was causing starvation in the Gaza Strip, according to Wafa.

Israel says the accusation is false and that food and supplies are in abundance. Israeli authorities have gradually eased the closure but still prevent tens of thousands of Palestinians from reaching jobs.
In the Gaza Strip, Israeli soldiers came under fire while on patrol near a Jewish settlement on Thursday.

"A Palestinian policeman was arrested this evening by soldiers after he fired at soldiers on routine patrol on the road separating Khan Younis and Gush Katif (settlement) in Gaza," the spokesman said.
Israel filed a complaint with Palestinian officials at a joint coordinating office in Gaza, most of which Israel handed over the PLO in 1994.
Palestinian Major General Abdel Razek al-Majayda said the four policemen were chasing a suspected smuggler who fired several shots in the air.
He said Israeli troops arrested one of the policemen and the suspect fled.
"We demand a joint investigation and the immediate release of the detained Palestinian policeman who never fired his gun," Majayda told Reuters.
In Jerusalem, an Israeli court sentenced to eight months in jail two paramilitary border policemen filmed beating Palestinians last October.

A Justice Ministry spokesman said several other border policemen were arrested on Thursday in connection with what Israel's Channel One television reported as another case of police brutality involving two Palestinian workers.
The television said the two were so badly beaten that they required hospital treatment.
